headline: Salesforce's Core/Advanced/Max editions are now live on one pricing page
old_price: Core, Advanced, Max announced Sept 3 with pricing described as taking effect "later this fall" — not yet shown as purchasable
new_price: Core $195/user/mo, Advanced $395/user/mo, Max $550/user/mo now live on Salesforce's Sales Cloud pricing page — Core/Advanced show "Try for free," Max shows "Contact us," same Flex Credits allotments as announced
body: The prices themselves haven't moved since the September 3 announcement. What changed is the status: Salesforce's Sales Cloud pricing page now lists Core, Advanced, and Max as active editions with the same figures as announced — $195/$395/$550 per user/month, billed annually, with 500,000/1,000,000/2,750,000 Flex Credits per org per year respectively. Core and Advanced carry "Try for free" buttons; Max requires contacting sales. One inconsistency: Salesforce's dedicated Agentforce pricing page (the source for our $125/mo add-on and Agentforce 1 Editions entries) still doesn't mention Core, Advanced, or Max by name — those editions currently live only on the Sales product pricing page. We could not confirm Salesforce's own claim that existing Agentforce 1 Edition customers get a free upgrade to Max, and no specific effective date is stated anywhere we checked. Both remain unconfirmed.

sources.name: Salesforce — Agentforce pricing page (Core/Advanced/Max not present)

takeaway: Core/Advanced/Max pricing has moved past the announcement stage: budget $195–$550/user/month depending on tier, and confirm with your rep which one applies to you.

headline: Salesforce adds Core/Advanced/Max Agentforce editions at $195–$550/user/mo
old_price: No fixed-credit Agentforce edition tiers — packaging was the $125/user/mo add-on plus consumption-based Flex Credits and Agentforce 1 Editions from $550/user/mo
new_price: Three new Agentforce Industry Editions — Core $195/user/mo (500,000 Flex Credits/org/year), Advanced $395/user/mo (1,000,000 Flex Credits/org/year), Max $550/user/mo (2,750,000 Flex Credits/org/year)
body: On September 3, 2026, Salesforce announced a new three-tier Agentforce Industry Edition structure: Core, Advanced, and Max. Each tier is priced per user per month and bundles a fixed amount of Flex Credits per org per year, rather than leaving credit usage entirely consumption-based. Salesforce says pricing on existing legacy editions is unchanged, and the new editions are rolling out "later this fall" rather than immediately. The announcement doesn't clarify how these relate to the Agentforce 1 Editions or the standalone $125/user/month add-on covered in our earlier entries. Whether they're replaced, renamed, or simply run alongside the new editions is unconfirmed, so we're not asserting a replacement here.
takeaway: These three tiers ($195/$395/$550 per user/month) now set the range for an Agentforce budget. Ask your rep which one maps to your current edition.

headline: Salesforce keeps Agentforce at $125/user/mo but adds new pricing models
new_price: $125/user/mo add-on remains, plus new Flex Credits ($500/100,000 credits), Conversations ($2 each), Agentforce 1 Editions (from $550/user/mo), and a $5/user/mo Agentforce User License
body: The $125/user/month Agentforce add-on hasn't been replaced; it's still listed for Sales and Service. What changed is the packaging around it: Salesforce now also sells consumption-based Flex Credits, per-conversation pricing, a much pricier all-in Agentforce 1 Edition tier, and a low-cost per-user license that still requires buying Flex Credits separately. For buyers, $125 is now one option inside a wider menu rather than the only current path to Agentforce.
takeaway: Already paying $125/user/month for Agentforce? That price doesn't change on its own. Check whether Flex Credits, per-conversation charges, or the $5 user license now apply to how your team actually uses it.

headline: Atlassian is sunsetting Data Center outright; Cloud migration isn't a like-for-like cost swap
verification_label: Current price verified · historical price third-party
old_price: Data Center: perpetual on-prem licensing, no defined end date
new_price: Phased shutdown: new-customer sales ended Mar 30, 2026 → existing-customer expansions end Mar 30, 2028 → licenses go read-only Mar 28, 2029
body: Atlassian is retiring Data Center entirely on a three-year phased timeline rather than just raising its price. Bitbucket Data Center is the one exception: it keeps a separate hybrid license instead of following the sunset schedule. Atlassian is offering a 10–20% first-year discount on Cloud Enterprise for customers who migrate by June 2027, but that incentive doesn't fully offset the underlying cost shift: independent analysis puts the average Cloud premium over equivalent Data Center pricing at around 28%, a figure Atlassian itself has not published or confirmed on its own pricing pages.
disputed_note: Atlassian does not publish or confirm this figure on its own pricing pages. The ~28% average Cloud cost premium comes from independent third-party analysis (Computerworld and The Jira Guy), not from Atlassian directly — treat it as a credible estimate, not a vendor-confirmed number.

sources.name: Atlassian — Data Center End of Life

takeaway: Teams running Data Center should start budgeting for Cloud now. The ~28% cost premium is a third-party estimate, not an Atlassian figure — get your own quote before assuming it holds for you.

headline: Salesforce replaces Einstein AI packaging with a $125/user/mo Agentforce add-on
body: This is an add-on price on top of the underlying Salesforce edition, not a replacement for Salesforce's core CRM subscription. Salesforce announced the Einstein-to-Agentforce replacement publicly in August 2025, so it's not a hidden pricing-page swap. The migration mechanics are where it gets less obvious: Agentforce (Default) reached End of Sale on June 17, 2025, and Salesforce's own Help docs lay out what happens when an existing Einstein customer upgrades their SKU to Agentforce. Separately, as of October 24, 2025, Agentforce usage outside unmetered employee-agent activity is tracked through a new "Flex Credits" system, so the $125/month sticker price doesn't mean unlimited AI usage. We could not verify a universal rule that every legacy Einstein customer is automatically moved to the new pricing at renewal; treat that specific claim as unconfirmed.

sources.name: Salesforce Help — Flex Credit Rate Card FAQ

takeaway: Still being quoted “Einstein” pricing? Ask your rep to confirm you're not paying for a retired SKU. Agentforce is the current name and price.

headline: QuickBooks raises affected Essentials, Plus, and Advanced subscriptions at renewal, not Simple Start
verification_label: Current price verified · historical price third-party
body: QuickBooks Online raised prices for Essentials, Plus, and Advanced at renewals on or after August 1, 2026. Simple Start, Free, Lite, and Ledger were not part of this increase, per QuickBooks' own announcement. Essentials rose to $85/mo (third-party sources disagree on the prior figure, citing either $60 or $75). Advanced rose to $340/mo (prior figure similarly disputed between $200 and $275 across sources). Prepaid annual subscribers generally keep their existing rate until the current term ends, and some recent subscribers get a six-month price-protection window. We could not source an exact count of how many total increases QuickBooks has made since 2022; treat "a series of past increases" as accurate without a specific number attached.
correction_note: An earlier version of this entry incorrectly stated that QuickBooks Simple Start's price rose to $38/mo on August 1, 2026. QuickBooks' own official pricing update confirms Simple Start, Free, Lite, and Ledger were explicitly excluded from this increase — only Essentials, Plus, and Advanced changed. This entry has been corrected to reflect that.
disputed_note: Third-party sources disagree on QuickBooks Plus's exact prior price — reports cite figures ranging roughly $99 to $115/mo, and no vendor archive confirms a single number. The current $140/mo figure is vendor-confirmed; only the historical 'before' price is disputed.

sources.name: MosoFin
sources.type: 3P — disagrees with Certum on prior Plus/Advanced figures

takeaway: Essentials, Plus, and Advanced subscribers should expect this increase at their next renewal. Simple Start, Free, Lite, and Ledger subscribers are unaffected.

headline: Figma's per-product pricing became per-seat, and monthly billing disappeared from Organization and Enterprise
old_price: Figma Design, Dev Mode, FigJam billed separately
new_price: Unified seat types (Full/Dev/Collab), $3–$90/seat/mo depending on plan and seat type
body: The bigger story isn't the sticker price: it's that Organization and Enterprise no longer offer monthly billing at all going forward, only annual. Teams with fluctuating headcount lost a flexibility option that existed before the overhaul, and it's easy to miss unless you're pricing out a renewal. Per-seat pricing (as of Sep 2026) breaks down as: Professional: Full $16/mo, Dev $12/mo, Collab $3/mo; Organization: Full $55/mo, Dev $25/mo, Collab $5/mo; Enterprise: Full $90/mo, Dev $35/mo, Collab $5/mo. Figma Design itself can't be purchased separately; it's bundled into the Full seat alongside Dev Mode, FigJam, and Figma Slides.
takeaway: Teams on an Organization or Enterprise plan lose monthly billing entirely — budget annually so renewal doesn't catch you off guard.

headline: Kit retired its old $15 entry tier; Creator now starts at $33/mo billed annually
verification_label: Current price verified · historical price third-party
body: This wasn't a gradual increase. The old low-tier pricing structure was retired outright in the September 2025 repricing, and anyone quoting Kit's "starts at $15" is quoting a price that no longer exists for new signups. Separately, as of September 2026, Kit's higher tier is mid-rebrand: its current marketing page is titled "Kit Pro," while the linked help-center article and the page's own URL slug still say "Creator Pro." At 1,000 subscribers, Pro currently starts at $79/month, or $66/month equivalent billed annually.

sources.name: Ecommerce-Platforms.com, published April 2024 — contemporaneous record of the $15/mo price while it was still current
Kit Pro marketing page
sources.type: VENDOR — Pro rebrand and current pricing

takeaway: Signed up for Kit before September 2025? Check your actual invoice. The old $15/month tier no longer exists for new signups and may not be honored at your next renewal either.
